stories.title: European shares hold near records as Siemens Energy and AI optimism lift sentiment
stories.dek: AI optimism and stronger corporate outlooks supported the regional benchmark, although inflation and rates remained a drag on sentiment.
body: European shares traded near record levels, with the STOXX 600 up 0.2% at 660.06 points by 1025 GMT, as upbeat company outlooks lifted technology and energy-related shares. The index was earlier reported up 0.7% at 0807 GMT.

The gains came despite hotter-than-expected US inflation and renewed rate-hike concerns. Siemens Energy rose 8.3% after raising its 2027 margin outlook and proposing to more than triple its dividend; CSG fell 18% after cutting its full-year operating-margin forecast.

sources.title: European stocks near record high on Siemens, CoreWeave AI optimism

stories.title: Hot US inflation and Fed warnings put a jumbo December hike on the radar
stories.dek: The inflation surprise and hawkish Fed rhetoric have shifted rate expectations sharply higher, even as equities rebounded on Wednesday.
body: A hotter-than-expected US October CPI report and hawkish Federal Reserve comments on Tuesday pushed investors to price in a December rate increase as nearly certain, with an outside chance of a 50-basis-point move. Fed Governor Christopher Waller had said a half-point rise should be considered if core monthly inflation was 0.3% or higher; October core CPI matched that threshold.
US two-year Treasury yields jumped nearly 19 basis points to 4.736% on Tuesday, while the 10-year yield rose to 4.99%. The US Treasury market is closed Wednesday for Veterans Day.

sources.title: Fed officials open door to a half-percentage-point rate hike as inflation worsens

stories.title: CoreWeave outlook sparks an AI-share rebound, with Nvidia among the gainers
stories.dek: CoreWeave’s profitability target revived demand for AI-linked shares after a bruising sell-off.
body: CoreWeave shares rose about 10% in US trading after strong results and a forecast that it would reach adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028. Its revenue growth and outlook helped ease concerns about whether demand could support its debt-funded expansion.

The results also lifted AI-linked shares: Nvidia was up about 5% in premarket trading after losing roughly $430 billion in market value over the prior two sessions. US index futures had rallied before the open, with Nasdaq 100 futures up nearly 2%.

sources.title: CoreWeave sparks AI cloud stock rally, lifts Nvidia as results ease bubble fears
S&P 500, Nasdaq futures rise as CoreWeave results calm AI jitters

stories.title: Brent rebounds as Hormuz shipping attacks temper hopes for an Iran de-escalation
stories.dek: Persistent shipping risks in the Gulf offset hopes of de-escalation and lifted benchmark crude prices.
body: Brent crude rose about 1.4% to $92.81 a barrel by 1314 GMT, recovering after a fall to two-month lows in the previous session. Traders weighed hopes of de-escalation in the Iran conflict against continued attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

Reuters reported 37 ships were attacked in the strait and nearby waters in October, the highest monthly total since the war began, and cited 10 attacks so far in November. The renewed oil rise added to inflation concerns in energy-importing Europe.

sources.title: Oil up 1% after Iran says no nuclear material will leave the country

stories.title: Siemens Energy lifts its margin outlook as data-centre demand boosts power equipment
stories.dek: Data-centre power demand is supporting the group’s margin ambitions, while its wind unit has reached break-even.
body: Siemens Energy said it expects its profit margin to rise to 14%-16% in 2027, from 12.4% in 2026, as data-centre construction boosts demand for gas turbines and grid equipment. It proposed a €2.30-per-share dividend for 2026, compared with €0.70 a year earlier.
The company also said its Siemens Gamesa wind division had reached break-even, a milestone after years of losses and restructuring. Siemens Energy shares gained 8.3% in European trading.

sources.title: Siemens Energy sees higher margins as data centres boost power equipment demand

stories.title: Vestas narrows its 2026 outlook after quarterly profit misses forecasts
stories.dek: A quarterly miss and narrower annual outlook overshadowed higher margins and service growth.
body: Vestas reported third-quarter EBIT before special items of €483 million, below analyst expectations of €526 million, while revenue of €5.68 billion also missed forecasts. The company narrowed its 2026 revenue outlook to €20.5 billion-€21.5 billion and its EBIT-margin range to 7.5%-8.5%.
Shares fell as much as 6% in European trading, with added operating costs at a European offshore project weighing on results. Vestas said service revenue grew 13.2% year on year.

sources.title: Vestas narrows 2026 outlook after quarterly profit misses estimates
Europe's STOXX 600 near record high as Siemens Energy, CoreWeave outlooks lift sentiment

stories.title: RWE beats nine-month earnings expectations on favourable wind conditions
stories.dek: Favourable wind conditions helped Germany’s largest power producer beat the market’s nine-month earnings forecast.
body: RWE reported adjusted core earnings of €4.58 billion for the first nine months of the year, above analyst expectations of €4.43 billion. Reuters attributed the outperformance to more favourable wind conditions.
The result adds to a busy European earnings session, with investors weighing corporate updates alongside inflation and energy-market risks.

sources.title: RWE posts 9-month core earnings above expectations on favourable conditions

stories.title: CSG slumps after cutting its operating-margin forecast
stories.dek: A lower profitability outlook and quarterly revenue miss made the defence group one of Europe’s sharpest decliners.
body: The Czech ammunition and arms producer cut its full-year operating-margin forecast, sending its shares down 18% in European trading. Reuters also reported that third-quarter revenue fell short of estimates.
The warning weighed on the broader European defence sector, even as the wider STOXX 600 advanced.

sources.title: Europe's STOXX 600 near record high as Siemens Energy, CoreWeave outlooks lift sentiment

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $74,000 as equity markets rebound and ETF outflows persist
stories.dek: Bitcoin steadied near $74,000 but did not join the AI-led equity rebound.
body: Bitcoin traded around $74,000 on Wednesday, little changed since midnight UTC, after dipping to $72,700 on Tuesday. Ether was near $2,050, while the CoinDesk 80 Index slipped 0.3%.

Crypto remained weaker than the rebound in US equity futures, with investors still digesting the hot US inflation report and ongoing ETF outflows. CoinDesk said bitcoin’s relative stability followed the prior day’s leverage flush-out.

stories.title: Dollar strength and Fed-hike bets keep currency markets mixed
stories.dek: Rate expectations supported the dollar, while the recovery in technology shares helped risk appetite elsewhere.
body: Markets were balancing a firmer dollar and expectations for higher US rates against improved risk appetite from the AI-driven equity bounce. Reuters reported emerging-market currencies traded mixed on Wednesday as the stronger dollar and higher-for-longer rate concerns pressured riskier assets.
A quarter-point Fed increase in December was being priced as nearly certain, with an approximately 11% chance of a half-point move, according to the Reuters report.

stories.title: Hot inflation sends US stocks lower and Treasury yields sharply higher
stories.dek: Hotter inflation drove a broad pullback in US equities and a sharp rise in Treasury yields.
body: US shares reversed Monday’s rally on Tuesday as the October inflation report reinforced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. The Dow fell 0.57% to 52,087.13, the S&P 500 lost 0.71% to 7,496.63 and the Nasdaq dropped 0.90% to 25,025.83.

Treasury yields climbed: the two-year yield rose about 19 basis points to 4.74%, while the 10-year yield gained about 13 basis points to 4.99%. Reuters reported markets were weighing the possibility of a half-point December increase.

Wall St falls as hot inflation data fuels rate-hike jitters

stories.title: Nvidia slide makes technology the weakest US sector
stories.dek: Rate concerns and a sharp Nvidia decline weighed on technology shares during the session.
body: Technology was the weakest major S&P 500 sector, falling 1.8%, while rate-sensitive real estate and utilities each lost more than 0.5%, Reuters reported during the session.
Nvidia fell 6.3% amid concerns following an internal probe into spy claims involving its CEO. The semiconductor index was down 1.9% in midday trading, with peers subdued after recent gains.

stories.title: Two-year Treasury yield posts its biggest daily jump since 2025
stories.dek: Short-dated borrowing costs surged as investors repriced the December rate outlook.
body: The two-year Treasury yield rose to 4.74%, its biggest one-day jump since the April 2025 tariff turmoil, Reuters reported. The 10-year yield rose to 4.988%.

The move followed inflation data that strengthened the case for another Fed rate increase. Fed Governor Christopher Waller had said he would support at least a quarter-point hike in December and would consider a half-point move if inflation worsened.

stories.title: Dollar rallies as hotter inflation lifts rate expectations
stories.dek: The dollar strengthened against major peers as markets reassessed the Fed path.
body: The dollar index rose 0.6% to 102.29 as investors responded to the inflation report and higher rate expectations. The euro fell 0.56% to $1.1156 and the dollar gained 0.5% against the yen to 158.68.
The dollar’s advance accompanied higher Treasury yields and a retreat in risk assets.

stories.title: Gold falls with higher yields as oil remains under pressure
stories.dek: Higher yields pressured gold, while crude extended its decline amid Iran diplomacy hopes.
body: Gold fell 2.3% to $4,043.73 an ounce as the dollar and Treasury yields rose after the inflation release, according to Reuters.
US crude slipped 1.39% to $85.67 a barrel and Brent fell 2.03% to $90.69. Oil remained under pressure as investors assessed prospects for talks between Washington and Tehran.

The DAX rose 0.31% and the CAC 40 gained 0.55%, while the FTSE 100 slipped 0.29%. European markets surrendered some earlier gains after the US inflation reading lifted rate-hike expectations.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips as ETF withdrawals extend and MARA discloses sales
stories.dek: Bitcoin lagged equities amid sustained ETF withdrawals and disclosed miner selling.
body: Bitcoin traded around $73,435, down 1.4% since midnight UTC, as it failed to join the rebound in US equities, CoinDesk reported.

US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $201 million in outflows on Monday, taking withdrawals since November 2 to about $1.5 billion. BlackRock’s IBIT saw its seventh consecutive session of redemptions. Miner MARA said it had sold 13,597 bitcoin for about $1.1 billion over six weeks and planned further sales.

The shortfall added to pressure on individual stocks as investors digested results alongside the inflation-driven market repricing.

stories.dek: Waller backed another December hike and left the door open to a larger move if inflation worsens.
body: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support a 25-basis-point rate increase at the December meeting even if inflation had improved. He said a worsening inflation picture could justify considering a half-point move.

Futures had priced an approximately 85% chance of a December hike before the October inflation release, Reuters reported. The data subsequently intensified market attention on the size of the next move.

body: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast, while core CPI increased 0.3%, also exceeding expectations. The hotter print strengthened bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase next month and weighed on US equity futures.

body: Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since August 31, extending losses after US President Donald Trump downplayed the prospect of further military action against Iran. At 0930 GMT, Brent was down 2.58% at $90.18 and WTI had fallen 2.43% to $84.74.

The chipmaker cited demand from data centres, power infrastructure and software-defined vehicles; other European chip stocks also advanced.

stories.dek: A stronger outlook was tempered by a downturn in Vodafone’s key German market.
body: Vodafone raised its full-year guidance after service-revenue growth accelerated in the first half, led by business-to-business operations and Africa. It now expects adjusted earnings of €13.2bn–€13.4bn and free cash flow of €2.8bn–€3.0bn; German service revenue turned negative, falling 0.5% in the second quarter. Shares were down 1.8% in early deals.

stories.dek: The French jobless rate edged down, but remained higher than a year earlier.
body: France’s ILO unemployment rate eased to 8.2% in the third quarter from 8.3% in the previous quarter, INSEE reported. The number of unemployed fell by 47,000 over the quarter to 2.6 million, though the rate remained 0.4 percentage points above its year-earlier level.

stories.title: US jobs jump 165,000, strengthening the case for higher rates
stories.dek: A stronger-than-expected jobs report reinforced bets on a December Fed rate increase and pushed Treasury yields higher.
body: US payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, well above the 65,000 expected in a Reuters poll, while September’s gain was revised up to 60,000 from 29,000. Unemployment edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%.

The stronger report lifted expectations of a December Fed rate increase: Reuters reported market-implied odds rose to 78% from 70%. Treasury yields initially rose; the two-year was up 5 basis points at 4.52% and the 10-year up 4 basis points at 4.88% in the report’s snapshot.

stories.title: European stocks slide as AI concerns deepen the global rout
stories.dek: European shares extended the global sell-off as investors reassessed AI investment and regulation risks.
body: The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 1% to 648.83 by 0919 GMT as the global technology sell-off weighed on shares. The decline erased the index’s gains for the week, leaving it down about 0.3% on the week at that point.
Investors worried that the Democrats’ control of Congress could bring tighter limits on AI data-centre spending, amid concerns about returns, valuations and debt-funded investment.

body: Teleperformance shares fell 18% after the outsourcing company cut its full-year revenue-growth outlook. Weakness in its trust and safety business outweighed growth in AI-powered and back-office services, Reuters reported.
The decline made the company one of the sharpest individual losers in the European session.

stories.title: Daimler Truck profit rises 73% as weaker orders temper the recovery
stories.dek: Profit surged on a North American recovery, though weaker order intake clouded the outlook for the truckmaker’s key market.
body: Daimler Truck reported third-quarter adjusted operating profit of €1.12 billion, up from €648 million a year earlier and slightly above the €1.10 billion company-compiled consensus. It confirmed its full-year outlook.

But group order intake missed Visible Alpha expectations by 9%, including a 16% shortfall in North America, its largest market by revenue. The North American unit’s adjusted operating margin improved to 12.1% from 6.4%.

The modest bounce followed Thursday’s sell-off, when more than $1 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours. US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded further outflows on Thursday, including about $200 million from Fidelity’s FBTC and $105 million from BlackRock’s IBIT.

The jobs report then sent Treasury yields higher and lifted rate-hike bets, complicating the rebound. Reuters’ market snapshot put the two-year Treasury yield up 5 basis points at 4.52%.

body: Global equity funds attracted inflows for a seventh consecutive week through November 4, with European equity funds taking in $13.25 billion, their largest weekly intake since August 12, Reuters reported, citing LSEG data.
The inflows came despite the week’s late risk-off move. Reuters linked demand for European funds in part to lower oil and natural-gas prices, which had eased inflation concerns.

stories.dek: Wall Street reversed its post-election rally as AI spending and data-centre concerns triggered a broad sell-off and pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory.
body: US stocks suffered a sharp reversal, wiping out much of Wednesday’s post-election rally as investors reassessed the outlook for AI investment and data-centre construction. Reuters reported the Dow down 2.2%, the S&P 500 down 3.4% and the Nasdaq down 5.2% during the session.
The Nasdaq fell more than 10% from its October record close, putting it in correction territory. The sell-off broadened beyond technology, but chip and AI-infrastructure shares bore the brunt.

stories.title: Primo Brands beats quarterly earnings forecast but flags softer EBITDA
stories.dek: Primo Brands beat the earnings estimate but warned that full-year EBITDA would likely reach only the bottom of its existing range.
body: Primo Brands reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.43 per share, above the cited analyst expectation of $0.37, on revenue of $1.82 billion, up 3.1% year on year.

The company kept its sales-growth and free-cash-flow outlooks, but said adjusted EBITDA was likely to land at the lower end of its $1.47 billion–$1.52 billion range. It also authorised a new $300 million share-repurchase programme.

stories.title: Arm’s modest outlook fails to steady shares amid chip rout
stories.dek: Arm topped quarterly estimates, but a near-consensus forecast offered little support amid the chip sell-off.
body: Arm reported fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share on revenue of $1.44 billion, both above the cited analyst estimates. Its forecast for the next quarter was close to consensus: revenue of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.56, plus or minus $0.04.
The modestly above-consensus outlook did little to reassure investors amid a wider chip-sector retreat; shares slipped about 3% in after-hours trading, according to Yahoo Finance.

stories.title: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% and signals further tightening may be needed
stories.dek: The BoE lifted rates to 4% and indicated another increase could follow if the conflict-driven inflation shock persists.
body: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4%, its first increase in more than three years, in an 8–1 vote. The dissenter, Catherine Mann, preferred a half-point increase to 4.25%.
The Bank warned that at least one more increase was likely if the US-Iran conflict continued, as policymakers weighed inflation pressures; consumer price inflation was 3.5% in September.

stories.title: Oil rebounds after midweek plunge as markets reassess Iran-war outlook
stories.dek: Oil bounced after a sharp midweek drop, while lower crude had supported bonds and weighed on the dollar.
body: Oil prices remained a key driver as investors assessed the US midterm result and the prospect of pressure on Washington to end the Iran conflict. Brent had fallen more than 8% on Wednesday to a two-month low below $100 a barrel, then rebounded more than 2.8% on Thursday, Reuters reported.

Lower oil had helped pull Treasury yields to two-month lows and weaken the dollar, while the euro traded near a one-month high against the dollar. The reversal in crude prices tempered the relief from the previous session.

Nasdaq futures slip on chip weakness; S&P 500 holds gains

stories.title: European stocks edge higher as mining gains offset technology weakness
stories.dek: Mining and steel shares supported Europe’s advance, while technology stocks remained under pressure.
body: European shares rose, with the STOXX 600 up 0.7% to 661.99 by 0905 GMT, close to a record high. Basic resources led, while technology lagged amid concerns that greater US scrutiny could slow data-centre and AI investment.
ArcelorMittal gained around 5% in the session after beating analysts’ third-quarter EBITDA forecast. The steelmaker reported EBITDA of $2.02 billion against a $1.96 billion consensus.

ArcelorMittal beats profit expectations as European market strengthens

stories.title: Rheinmetall slumps after cutting its sales outlook for a second time
stories.dek: A second 2026 forecast cut sent Rheinmetall sharply lower as key programme and ammunition revenues were delayed.
body: Rheinmetall fell 14% in early European trading after cutting its 2026 sales forecast for the second time in three months. The company said it no longer expected a contract award this year for Germany’s Arminius Boxer vehicle programme and that artillery-ammunition revenue would be delayed by slower batch approvals.
The setback contrasted with the broader market’s gains and put pressure on the defence group’s outlook.

sources.title: European shares rise on mining gains; tech lags

stories.title: Air France-KLM jumps on earnings beat and €1 billion KLM savings plan
stories.dek: A profit beat and KLM cost-cutting plan lifted the airline group, despite a higher fuel-cost forecast.
body: Air France-KLM shares rose about 13% in early Paris trading after the group posted third-quarter operating profit of €1.34 billion, ahead of the €1.1 billion analyst consensus.

KLM announced a restructuring plan intended to improve annual earnings by €1 billion and said it would further reduce its workforce by nearly 15% over coming years. The group lowered its 2026 capacity-growth forecast to 2% and raised its expected fuel bill to $9.2 billion.

sources.title: Air France-KLM beats profit forecasts as KLM flags further cost cuts

stories.title: US jobless claims fall to a 57-year low ahead of payrolls report
stories.dek: New US unemployment claims hit a 57-year low, signalling continued resilience in the labour market.
body: US initial jobless claims fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 in the week to October 31, the lowest level in 57 years, as layoffs remained limited.
Continuing claims rose by 23,000 to 1.718 million. The weekly claims data fall outside the survey period for Friday’s closely watched October payrolls report.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims at 57-year lows amid low layoffs

stories.title: Qualcomm slides as weak handset-chip sales outlook drags on tech futures
stories.dek: A weak smartphone-chip outlook weighed on Qualcomm and added to the technology sector’s premarket losses.
body: Qualcomm shares fell about 10% in premarket trading after its forecast for fourth-quarter smartphone-chip sales fell short of Wall Street expectations. Reuters cited sluggish handset demand and declining Apple-related revenue as concerns for the company’s core business.
The weakness added to pressure on chip and data-centre stocks, with Nasdaq futures down while Dow futures rose before the open.

sources.title: S&P 500 futures steady after midterm rally; Nasdaq lags on chip weakness

stories.title: AppLovin jumps as Snap and Fair Isaac fall after results disappoint
stories.dek: Results misses hit Snap and Fair Isaac, while AppLovin rallied on a profit beat.
body: Pre-market moves were sharp among US companies reporting results: Snap fell 10.1% after missing third-quarter revenue estimates, while Fair Isaac dropped 9% after missing fourth-quarter profit estimates.
AppLovin rose 16.4% after beating third-quarter profit estimates. The moves came as Nasdaq futures lagged broader US index futures following the previous session’s rally.

sources.title: S&P 500 futures steady after midterm rally; Nasdaq lags on chip weakness

stories.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,000 as risk appetite returns
stories.dek: Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 as the crypto market joined the broader risk-asset rebound.
body: Bitcoin traded back above $80,000 as crypto assets recovered from several sessions of heavy selling. A Yahoo Finance report put bitcoin near $80,518, up about 4.7% over 24 hours, with ether up almost 7% to around $2,420.
The rebound followed increased risk appetite after the US midterm result; weaker dollar and Treasury yields had also supported crypto prices.

Bitcoin gains to $80.3k as U.S. elections buoy risk appetite, but outlook unclear

stories.title: US stocks rallied after Democrats’ sweep eased election uncertainty.
stories.dek: US equities climbed in a broad post-election rally, although energy shares fell as crude weakened.
body: US stocks rallied as investors responded to Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress, easing uncertainty about the election outcome. The Dow rose 2.89%, the S&P 500 gained 1.85% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 2.13%.

Communication services, consumer discretionary and consumer staples led gains, while energy was the weakest S&P 500 sector as oil prices fell. Investors also weighed the prospect of greater scrutiny of AI infrastructure and data-centre investment.

sources.title: Stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats' midterm sweep

stories.title: Treasury yields edged higher after reversing an early election-driven drop.
stories.dek: Treasuries reversed some early gains as investors weighed the election result and services data.
body: US Treasury yields were choppy as investors assessed the election result and economic data. Reuters reported the 10-year yield up 0.6 basis point to 4.956%, the 30-year up 1.1 basis points to 5.335%, and the two-year up 1.7 basis points to 4.631%.
Yields had fallen earlier as the election results came in, before paring the decline. October services-sector growth slowed marginally, while supply chains remained strained, Reuters reported.

sources.title: Treasuries-US bond yields rise as investors assess economic data, Democrat election victory

stories.title: Oil’s decline dragged energy shares lower as Iran-policy uncertainty returned.
stories.dek: Crude weakness weighed on energy shares as markets considered the election’s implications for Iran policy.
body: Oil prices fell as investors reassessed the outlook for the Iran war and the political constraints facing the White House after the Democratic victory. Reuters said energy shares were the biggest losers in the US market as crude weakened.
The move adds to uncertainty around energy supply and inflation, with the geopolitical outlook still a key influence on oil.

sources.title: Stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats' midterm sweep
Democratic sweep adds new twist to markets' Iran, AI, and debt worries

stories.title: European shares closed at a two-month high as banks surged.
stories.dek: European shares finished at a more than two-month high, led by banks.
body: The pan-European STOXX 600 rose 1.82% to 657.40, its highest close since August 26 and its biggest one-day advance since June 12, Reuters reported. The move followed broad gains after the US election result.
Eurozone banks led sectors, climbing 4.6%; Spain’s lender-heavy benchmark rose 3%. The gains extended the earlier European rebound rather than marking a new development in the day’s macro data.

sources.title: European shares jump over 1% after Democrats sweep US Congress, Novo Nordisk surges

stories.title: The dollar weakened after the Democratic election sweep.
stories.dek: The dollar fell as investors reassessed the implications of divided government.
body: The dollar weakened after Democrats won control of Congress, while the euro and sterling benefited, according to Reuters. Investors considered whether divided government could constrain abrupt policy changes and alter the outlook for trade and geopolitical policy.
The currency move came alongside a broad global equity rally, though Reuters noted that investors remained alert to continued volatility.

sources.title: Stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats' midterm sweep

stories.title: Consumer and communications shares outpaced energy in the US rally.
stories.dek: Consumer and communications shares helped lead the rally while energy fell with crude.
body: The election rally favoured consumer-facing shares, while energy stocks lagged. Reuters identified communication services, consumer discretionary and consumer staples as drivers of US gains, with energy the biggest sector loser as crude prices declined.
The contrasting performance reflected both a broad increase in risk appetite and a sharp sector-specific reaction to lower oil prices and changing expectations for policy.

sources.title: Stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats' midterm sweep

stories.title: Duolingo lifted its revenue forecast as user growth accelerated.
stories.dek: Duolingo raised its annual revenue outlook as user growth lifted shares despite a sharp profit drop.
body: Duolingo reported third-quarter revenue of $309 million, up 13.7% year over year, and daily active users rose 29% to 64.9 million. It raised its full-year revenue outlook to $1.22 billion from $1.21 billion, while quarterly profit fell sharply.
Shares surged more than 15% in premarket trading, with investors focusing on user growth and the higher revenue outlook despite the profit decline.

sources.title: Duolingo's stock soared 15%. Why weren't investors deterred by the plunge in earnings?

stories.title: Datadog fell as its fourth-quarter outlook disappointed investors.
stories.dek: A cautious fourth-quarter revenue outlook overshadowed Datadog’s strong quarterly beat.
body: Datadog’s third-quarter revenue grew 35% to $1.20 billion, and adjusted earnings of $0.81 a share beat expectations, according to its results. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1.19 billion to $1.20 billion, a range that disappointed investors.
Shares fell about 13% in regular trading, as the softer near-term outlook outweighed the quarterly beat and higher full-year revenue guidance.

sources.title: Datadog Sinks 13% as Flat Q4 Revenue Outlook Overshadows Earnings Beat

stories.title: Amdocs slumped after warning of a steep fiscal 2027 revenue decline.
stories.dek: Amdocs’ steep revenue outlook cut and contract dispute with T-Mobile drove a sharp share decline.
body: Amdocs forecast fiscal 2027 revenue to decline 14.3% to 17.9%, citing a contract dispute with T-Mobile, according to reported company news. Its shares fell sharply during the regular session as investors reacted to the outlook.
The forecast stood in contrast to the day’s broader risk-on tone and made Amdocs one of the largest single-stock decliners reported.

stories.title: Bitcoin recovered above $79,000 after an election-night slide.
stories.dek: Bitcoin rebounded above $79,000 after an election-night dip toward $75,600.
body: Bitcoin recovered after touching about $75,600 during election-result trading, later moving back above $79,000, according to market coverage. The rebound accompanied the broader improvement in risk appetite as the election outcome became clearer.
The recovery followed a brief sell-off that had taken the cryptocurrency to a multi-week low; price movements remained closely tied to the shifting political and market reaction.

stories.title: Eurozone inflation rises to a three-year high of 4.0%.
stories.dek: An energy-led rise in prices is keeping rate-hike risks in focus.
body: Eurozone inflation accelerated to 4.0% in October from 3.8% in September, its highest rate in three years, according to flash data reported on Wednesday. Higher energy prices were cited as the driver, adding to expectations of further European Central Bank tightening.

sources.title: Eurozone Inflation Accelerates To 3-Year High On Energy Prices

stories.title: Eurozone growth slowed to a four-month low in October.
stories.dek: Expansion persisted, but demand nearly stalled as cost pressures intensified.
body: The eurozone composite PMI fell to 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September, a four-month low and below the preliminary 51.9 reading. The services PMI eased to 51.4 from 53.0, while input-price inflation reached a five-month high and business confidence weakened.

stories.title: UK services growth reached an eight-month high, while cost pressures rose.
stories.dek: Activity improved, but rising costs complicate the outlook ahead of the BoE decision.
body: UK services activity strengthened: the October PMI rose to 52.8 from 52.1, its highest reading since February, while the composite index increased to 52.9 from 52.0. The services figure was below the flash estimate of 53.1; input-price inflation accelerated to its highest since May, adding to expectations of Bank of England tightening.

stories.title: European stocks rebounded as banks and clean-energy shares outperformed.

body: European shares recovered from early losses as investors assessed the US midterm result. The STOXX 600 was up 0.5% at 0816 GMT, with banks gaining more than 2%; clean-energy stocks also advanced, including Ørsted, up 7%, and Vestas, up 5%. Novo Nordisk rose after lifting its annual outlook.

Third-quarter adjusted operating profit was 31.72 billion Danish crowns, above the 28.39 billion analyst consensus; Wegovy pill sales were 5.39 billion crowns. Shares rose as much as 6.6% in early trading.

stories.title: AMD rallied in premarket after forecasting faster growth through 2027.
stories.dek: The outlook offered investors evidence that AI infrastructure demand extends beyond accelerator chips.

Third-quarter data-centre revenue rose 97% to $8.55 billion, beating expectations of $8.20 billion. The stock was up 7.3% in premarket trading.

stories.title: BMW’s quarterly pretax earnings fell 11% as China sales weakened.
stories.dek: Weak China sales and restructuring costs cloud the outlook despite an in-line earnings result.
body: BMW reported third-quarter pretax earnings of €2.1 billion, down 11% year on year and in line with analysts’ expectations. Revenue fell 6% to €30.4 billion, with declining sales in China weighing on results; the automotive operating margin narrowed to 3.4% from 5.2% a year earlier. The company also warned restructuring costs would hit later-year results.

stories.title: Fresenius raised its 2026 earnings expectations after a strong quarter.

It now expects constant-currency core EPS growth at the upper end of its 10%-15% range and an EBIT margin above 11.5%. Third-quarter EBIT before special items was €638 million, above the €618.5 million consensus.

stories.title: Iran strikes revive oil-market nerves after Monday’s plunge

body: Brent crude rebounded above $100 a barrel after the previous session’s roughly 7% drop, as reports of US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island unsettled markets and cast doubt on the prospects for de-escalation. The strikes were described by US officials as defensive.
The renewed tension around the Strait of Hormuz put energy supply risks back in focus as investors also watched for developments in US-Iran talks.

stories.title: European stocks slip as tech fears meet renewed Iran tensions

ASML and STMicroelectronics were among the tech stocks under pressure. Drax stood out, rising 9% after announcing a partnership to develop a data centre project that could attract more than £20 billion in investment.

stories.title: Bayer raises 2026 profit outlook on pharma strength
stories.dek: Stronger pharmaceutical performance prompted the German group to lift its full-year earnings range.
body: Bayer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to €9.8 billion–€10.3 billion from €9.6 billion–€10.1 billion, citing better-than-expected pharmaceutical performance. Its pharma business recorded third-quarter sales of €4.68 billion, 5% above analysts’ expectations in a Vara Research poll.

The group also lowered its expected year-end net financial debt range by €1 billion, to €28 billion–€29 billion. Its crop-science division’s adjusted core earnings were €101 million, below analysts’ €164 million estimate.

stories.title: AB Foods warns of another profit decline as sugar losses deepen
stories.dek: Lower Primark profitability and deeper sugar losses dragged on earnings, with another profit decline forecast.
body: Associated British Foods reported adjusted operating profit of £1.508 billion for the year to September 12, down 13% in reported currency and 14% at constant currency. Revenue was £19.58 billion, down 1% at constant currency, while adjusted earnings per share fell 11% to 156.0p.

The Primark owner expects adjusted operating profit and adjusted EPS to fall again in 2026/27, mainly because of its sugar business. Sugar recorded a £47 million loss in the year just ended, and ABF expects that loss to widen to £70 million–£170 million.

stories.title: Philips beats on adjusted profit and reaches preliminary DOJ agreement

body: Philips said third-quarter adjusted EBITA rose 7.2% to €569 million, ahead of analysts’ €522 million estimate, while comparable sales increased 3% to €4.39 billion, slightly below forecasts.

The company also reached a preliminary agreement with the US Department of Justice to resolve investigations connected to its 2021 global recall of sleep and respiratory-care devices. Philips reiterated its 2026 financial targets.

The weakness added to investor concerns about profitability across big technology companies, even as markets awaited US midterm election results.

stories.title: Bitcoin extends losses to a one-month low near $76,500

body: Bitcoin traded near $76,500 in early trading, down about 2% and at its lowest level in more than a month, as caution ahead of the US midterms added to pressure on digital assets.

The market was also contending with the fallout from the reported $6.3 billion Binance theft and recent outflows from spot bitcoin funds. Binance said it would cover customer losses and had resumed withdrawals at a staggered pace.

stories.title: AI spending fears deepen the global tech selloff

body: European shares fell as renewed concern about returns on heavy AI investment weighed on technology stocks. The STOXX 600 was down around 0.3% in morning trading, though it remained on track for a monthly gain.
US futures also pointed lower, with S&P 500 e-minis down 0.89% in Reuters’ morning report. After the open, the S&P 500 fell 1.16% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.26%, while the Dow edged up 0.08%.

Nasdaq tumbles at open as Amazon, Intel add to AI spending woes

stories.title: Euro-zone growth beats forecasts as inflation risks persist
stories.dek: The bloc’s growth beat expectations, but uneven national results and rising price pressures cloud the policy picture.
body: Euro-zone GDP grew 0.4% quarter on quarter in the third quarter, slowing from 0.6% in the previous quarter but exceeding the 0.2% growth economists had forecast.

Germany expanded 0.2%, Spain and the Netherlands each grew 0.6%, Italy was flat and France contracted 0.1%. Separate national inflation readings showed price growth accelerating in several major euro-zone economies, complicating the outlook for the ECB.

sources.title: Euro zone growth beats projections again

stories.title: German inflation cools more than expected
stories.dek: A larger-than-expected slowdown in German prices offered some relief amid wider euro-area inflation concerns.
body: Germany’s harmonised inflation rate slowed to 2.8% year on year in October, from 3.3% in September and below the 3.1% expected by economists polled by Reuters.
The first month of a fuel-tax cut helped ease pump-price pressures. Core inflation also declined, to 2.1% from 2.4%.

sources.title: German inflation slows more than expected in October

stories.title: ECB survey finds more euro-zone firms anticipate wage pressure
stories.dek: The survey adds to the ECB’s focus on whether the energy-driven inflation rise will feed into wages.
body: The ECB’s quarterly survey of large euro-zone companies found that 40% expected or saw a risk of higher wage demands, up from 20% in the previous survey in July.

Companies still expected wage growth to slow, from 3.2% last year to 3.0% this year and 2.9% next year, but at a more gradual pace than previously anticipated. The survey also pointed to continued cost pressures, including from energy and agricultural prices.

sources.title: Euro zone companies brace for higher wage demands, ECB poll shows

stories.title: US labour costs rise at a slower pace in the third quarter
stories.dek: A moderation in quarterly labour-cost growth offered a counterpoint to recent US inflation concerns.
body: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, matching economists’ expectations but slowing from a 0.9% increase in the second quarter, according to the Employment Cost Index.
Wages and salaries rose 0.7% in the quarter, also slower than the prior period. Total labour costs were up 3.4% over the year to September, while inflation-adjusted wages fell 0.6%.

sources.title: Slower wage growth curbs US labor costs in third quarter

stories.title: BP posts $8.46 billion quarterly profit and reaches debt target early
stories.dek: Higher energy prices and refining margins lifted BP’s profit to a record under its current reporting measure.
body: BP reported third-quarter underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.46 billion, above the $7.33 billion expected by analysts and up from $2.2 billion a year earlier. The company said its quarterly operating cash flow was $14.8 billion.

Net debt fell to $13.9 billion, allowing BP to reach its net-debt target a year early. The company said it would use the windfall to settle its remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities; its shares were up about 0.5% in morning trading.

sources.title: BP beats third-quarter forecasts with record $8.46 billion profit

Third-quarter business operating income was €5.43 billion, ahead of the €4.32 billion analyst consensus cited by Reuters. The French drugmaker’s shares rose nearly 6% to their highest level since April as it also signalled interest in acquisitions to replenish its pipeline.

Reuters’ European-market report put the shares up 4% in one update; a later market report recorded a gain of 6.9%.

body: Bayer rose after winning a trial on Thursday involving claims by three women that its Roundup weedkiller caused their cancer. Reuters reported the shares up 4.1% in European trading.
The court outcome offered a positive legal development for the company as investors weighed ongoing litigation exposure.

stories.title: Binance says partners have located about $3 billion in affected assets
stories.dek: Asset freezes covered roughly half the reported haul, but crypto prices remained under pressure as the recovery picture stayed incomplete.

Bitcoin reached a six-week low and was last down about 3% in Reuters’ market update, while ether was down more than 3%. Reuters also reported that stablecoin issuers had frozen roughly half of the stolen assets.

stories.title: Intel sinks about a quarter as a PC slump and weak outlook overshadow AI growth
stories.dek: Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $15–16bn came in well below the roughly $17.1bn analysts expected.
body: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15bn–$16bn, below both the third quarter’s $16.5bn and the consensus of about $17.1bn. It expects adjusted gross margin to fall to 38% from 44.1%, and adjusted EPS of about $0.25 against roughly $0.43 expected.

PC revenue fell 5% to $8.1bn while data-centre and AI revenue rose 78%. Management said PC weakness would last at least through the first half of next year, and also pointed to a factory accident in Israel.
The shares were down about 25% before the US open, dragging chipmakers in Asia and Europe lower.

stories.title: Amazon misses on earnings as AI spending pushes free cash flow negative
stories.dek: AWS grew 39%, but trailing free cash flow swung to about minus $42.4bn.
body: Third-quarter sales rose 12% to $201.9bn and AWS grew 39%, but earnings per share of $1.89 missed the $1.96 estimate and sales were slightly light.
Trailing twelve-month free cash flow turned negative at about −$42.4bn as Amazon lifted its 2026 capital spending plan to around $220bn, much of it on AI infrastructure.
The shares fell about 7% before the open, feeding the wider debate over whether AI capex is earning a return.

stories.title: Binance hit by an estimated $6.3bn hack, likely crypto’s largest theft
stories.dek: About $3bn has been frozen; Binance says it will cover all losses and reopen withdrawals within two days.
body: Binance halted withdrawals after attackers drained an estimated $6.3bn. Around $3bn has been frozen with blockchain partners and law enforcement, and investigators have linked the attack to North Korea.
The exchange first pointed to a compromised employee laptop, then said it had found further points of breach. It has set aside about $6.34bn to make customers whole and says deposits were unaffected.
Bitcoin dropped below $77,000 and ether fell nearly 6%, with roughly $1.5bn of leveraged positions liquidated.

stories.title: Brent climbs toward $118 as tanker attacks keep Hormuz risk alive
stories.dek: Iran claimed mine strikes on commercial vessels even as Washington said the war would end soon.
body: Brent rose about 2.5% to near $117.80 a barrel and WTI to about $104 after reports of attacks on tankers and Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Arabia.
President Trump said the conflict with Iran would end soon without saying how, while US Central Command said southern shipping lanes were open. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran.
Traders are also weighing the risk of renewed fighting around the 3 November US midterm elections.

stories.title: AstraZeneca beats third-quarter forecasts and keeps full-year guidance
stories.dek: Pre-tax profit rose 22% to $3.96bn on revenue of $16.21bn.
body: Revenue rose 6.7% to $16.21bn and pre-tax profit climbed 22% to $3.96bn, both ahead of market expectations. Full-year guidance was unchanged.
The shares rose almost 4%, one of the main supports for the FTSE 100 on a weak day for growth stocks elsewhere.

stories.title: NatWest falls 7% as net interest income misses and AI-led job cuts reach 1,400
stories.dek: Attributable profit slipped 4.1% to £1.53bn; the full-year outlook was kept.
body: Net interest income rose 8.9% to £3.56bn but missed analyst forecasts, and profit attributable to shareholders fell 4.1% to £1.53bn.
The bank said about 1,400 roles have gone this year, around 1,000 of them in the quarter, as AI changes how it operates. Its full-year outlook was reaffirmed.
NatWest was the biggest drag on the FTSE 100 by midday.

stories.title: Mobico agrees £308m cash takeover by Leita Mobility at a 55% premium
stories.dek: The 46p-a-share offer values the bus and coach operator at about £2.32bn including debt.
body: Mobico backed a cash offer of 46p a share from Leita Mobility, part of Spain’s Autobuses de León, a 55% premium to the 20 October close of 29.7p.
Including debt, the deal values the group at around £2.32bn. It is expected to complete through a court-sanctioned scheme. The shares rose about 12%.

stories.title: Sandisk falls despite a revenue beat and an eight-for-one split
stories.dek: Investors worry memory pricing is close to a peak.
body: Fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 23% to $11.03bn, above the company’s own forecast, and Sandisk announced an eight-for-one stock split.
The shares still fell nearly 8% before the open as investors questioned how long strong memory prices can last.

stories.title: Reddit and Twilio slump on softer outlooks
stories.dek: Reddit’s US daily users fell 2% despite 53% revenue growth; Twilio guided growth lower.
body: Reddit grew revenue 53% and beat on earnings, but a weaker fourth-quarter revenue outlook and a 2% drop in US daily active users sent the shares down more than 20%.
Twilio guided fourth-quarter revenue growth to 17%–17.5% after 20% in the third quarter, and fell around 20% before the open.

stories.title: France’s economy shrinks 0.1% as inflation rises to 3.4%
stories.dek: The 10-year OAT yield rose to about 4.97%.
body: French GDP fell 0.1% in the third quarter while inflation climbed to 3.4%, a stagflationary mix that pushed the 10-year OAT yield up to about 4.97%.

stories.title: BT jumps on report Virgin Media O2 is close to an Openreach fibre deal
stories.dek: Neither company has confirmed the talks.
body: BT rose almost 6% after reports that Virgin Media O2 is nearing an agreement to use Openreach’s fibre network outside its own footprint, while pausing some of its own cable upgrades to save costs. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

stories.title: Alphabet has its worst day on record after an earnings miss
stories.dek: Adjusted EPS of $2.12 missed consensus by about 28%; free cash flow was about −$9.1bn.
body: Search revenue of $63.4bn fell short of the $64.9bn expected, and free cash flow came in at about −$9.1bn against −$3.5bn forecast. The shares fell 12.6%, pulling the Nasdaq down 1.4%.

stories.title: ServiceNow and Fortinet tumble on soft forward indicators
stories.dek: ServiceNow posted its worst day on record.
body: ServiceNow fell 27% after guiding fourth-quarter remaining performance obligation growth to 18.5% against 19.4% expected. Fortinet dropped 20% after trimming its full-year service revenue forecast below consensus.

stories.title: US economy grew 3.4% annualised in Q3; core PCE rose 0.3%
stories.dek: Growth beat the 3.2% estimate while monthly core inflation came in below forecast.
body: Third-quarter GDP beat the 3.2% estimate. Core PCE rose 0.3% in September, below the 0.4% forecast, for 3.1% year on year, while headline PCE ran at 3.6%. Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000.

stories.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4% as two officials vote for a hike
stories.dek: Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favour of tightening.
body: The Federal Reserve under Chair Kevin Warsh left its target range at 3.75%–4%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voting for an increase. After the press conference, futures priced a December hike at close to 90%.
